title: Understand negative numbers on a number line and in context (temperature, elevation, money)

lesson.title: Numbers Below Zero

steps.say: You already know how to compare and order numbers like twelve and twenty. But on a cold January morning in Kamloops the radio says it is five degrees below zero, and your bank app says negative eight dollars. Today we figure out what those numbers below zero actually mean.

Think of a number line as a thermometer lying on its side. Zero sits in the middle. Every number to the right of zero is above zero, and every number to the left of zero is below zero. We write those left ones with a little minus sign in front, like negative five. So negative five degrees means five steps colder than zero.

visual.caption: Negative five sits five steps to the LEFT of zero

steps.say: Negative numbers show up all over real life. Zero can mean sea level, so a scuba diver six metres under the water in Howe Sound is at negative six metres. Zero can mean an empty account, so owing your friend six dollars for a bubble tea puts you at negative six dollars. Same spot on the line, three different stories.

visual.caption: Negative six: six metres under water, or six dollars owed

steps.say: Here is the trap almost everyone falls into. On Grouse Mountain it was negative two degrees at lunch and negative seven degrees at night. Lots of kids say negative seven is bigger, because seven is bigger than two. But look at the line! Negative seven is way out to the LEFT of negative two, and left always means smaller. So negative seven is actually less than negative two. It is the colder, deeper, more owing number.

visual.caption: Negative seven is left of negative two, so it is SMALLER

steps.say: So the rule is simple: forget the size of the digits and just look at where the number sits. Further left on the line, further below zero, always smaller.

visual.caption: Left is smaller, right is bigger — always

lesson.answer: On a number line, further LEFT means smaller — so negative seven is less than negative two, even though seven looks bigger.

practice.question: Draw your own number line from negative ten to positive ten, with zero in the middle. On Monday morning in Prince George it was negative three degrees, and on Tuesday morning it was negative eight degrees. Mark both temperatures on your line. Which morning was colder, and which of the two numbers is the bigger number?
practice.answer: Tuesday was colder, because negative eight is further to the left of zero. And negative three is the bigger number, since it sits to the right of negative eight — we write negative eight is less than negative three.
